written.myAnswer: A system is a group of interrelated components that work together to achieve an objective. Its basic components are objectives, components, environment, and communication.
Natural systems occur in nature, while artificial systems are designed and created by humans to serve a purpose.
A computer system consists of hardware, software, data, users, and procedures that work together to process data and produce useful information.
Computing systems include computers that process data, software systems that provide instructions or services, networks that connect computers, and the Internet, a worldwide network of networks.
The main components are memory, the Control Unit, the Arithmetic Logic Unit, input, and output. The Control Unit and Arithmetic Logic Unit form the CPU.
The Von Neumann architecture stores program instructions and data in the same memory. Its main components are memory, the CPU (Control Unit and Arithmetic Logic Unit), input, and output units.
The Von Neumann bottleneck is the limit on data and instruction transfer caused by their sharing a memory and data path between memory and the CPU.
Programs can be stored in memory and modified, making the system flexible and easier to program.
A computing system requires hardware, software, and electrical power to function.

A system is a group of related components that interact to achieve an objective. Its components carry out functions, its environment consists of the surrounding elements that can affect it, and communication links allow its components to exchange information.

Natural systems arise in nature, such as the solar system or a human body. Artificial systems are designed and made by people to meet needs, such as a computer system or transport system. Both contain interacting components that perform functions.

Natural science uses systems theory to study interacting parts of natural phenomena, such as an ecosystem. Design science uses it to design and improve purposeful systems, such as a transport system. Computer science applies it to develop and understand computing systems, such as computers and networks.
Computers process data; software systems provide programs and services; computer networks connect devices to share data and resources; and the Internet is a global network connecting networks.
A computer system aims to process data into useful information. Its hardware, software, data, users, and procedures interact through input, processing, storage, and output.

The Von Neumann architecture stores instructions and data in the same memory. Input and output units communicate with the computer, memory stores data and instructions, and the CPU (CU and ALU) controls and performs processing. In the instruction cycle, the CPU fetches an instruction from memory, decodes it, executes it, and stores the result.

A computer receives input from its environment, such as a user typing on a keyboard; it can exchange data over a network, such as sending or receiving a file; and it uses electrical power to operate. It also sends information back to the environment through output devices, such as displaying results on a screen.

The user requests the file, and the operating system directs the storage device to retrieve it. The file data is transferred over the system bus into memory. The CPU and relevant software process or interpret the data, and the computer sends the resulting display information to the monitor.
